newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rose to 11.8 vs 10.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rose to 11.8 vs 10.7 pct.

text.p: Increased volume of term loans pushed Croatian average lending rate to 11.8 percent on Wednesday from 10.7 percent in lively trade.
Total settlements rose to 41.3 million kuna compared to 25 million on Tuesday, but were still overshot by 56 million kuna in supply. All but 17.5 million were fresh borrowings.
A large two-week loan, made at 13 percent accounted for most of term loans.
One smaller deal was made at 26 percent raising the weighted call money rate to 11.6 percent from 10.5 on Tuesday.
Insurers rolled over one-week funds at seven percent and one-month loans at 13 percent. Banks renewed old deals at 12 percent for one-week and 14 percent for one-month borrowings.
National bank's kuna midrates for Thursday were firmer at 6.0279 against the dollar and at 3.5651 versus German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
